content.user_title: Send Java Logs to Azure Monitor
content.value_statement: Java teams need reliable guidance for sending custom logs to Azure Monitor. This skill explains SDK setup, DCR configuration, uploads, error handling, and throughput options.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for azure-monitor-ingestion.
Explains required Data Collection Endpoint, rule, stream, and workspace inputs.
Provides synchronous and asynchronous Java client setup guidance.
Demonstrates custom log upload patterns with batching and concurrency options.
Covers upload error handling and partial failure handling.
Links to official Azure SDK and Azure Monitor documentation.
limitations: Does not create Azure resources or Data Collection Rules automatically.
Requires valid Azure permissions and configured credentials outside the skill.
Examples need adaptation to each workspace schema and table design.
Does not validate live ingestion behavior or Log Analytics query results.

use_cases.title: Add Application Log Ingestion
use_cases.description: Use the Java SDK to send custom application events into Azure Monitor through an existing DCR.

use_cases.title: Standardize Observability Setup
use_cases.description: Document endpoint, rule, stream, and table inputs for repeatable Azure Monitor ingestion across services.

use_cases.title: Improve Upload Reliability
use_cases.description: Apply batching, concurrency, and partial failure handling for higher volume custom log uploads.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the Maven dependency, Azure inputs, and Java client setup for Azure Monitor log ingestion.

prompt_templates.title: Create Upload Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to describe a Java upload flow for custom logs using my DCR ID, stream name, and endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Upload Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design error handling for partial upload failures and HTTP errors in Azure Monitor ingestion.

prompt_templates.title: Tune High Volume Ingestion
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend batching, concurrency, and async client choices for high volume Java log ingestion.

output_examples.input: I need to send Java service logs to Azure Monitor.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist covering Maven dependency, Azure endpoint, DCR ID, stream name, credential setup, and a basic upload flow.

output_examples.input: My uploads may contain many log records.
output_examples.output: A throughput plan that uses batching, max concurrency, reusable clients, and partial failure handling.

output_examples.input: Azure Monitor returns authorization or not found errors.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path that checks DCR permissions, endpoint correctness, rule ID, stream name, and table schema alignment.

best_practices: Batch log entries and reuse the ingestion client for repeated uploads.
Keep DCR stream names, table schemas, and log fields aligned.
Handle partial failures and authorization errors before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real tenant secrets, client secrets, or access tokens in examples.
Do not send sensitive application data without a retention and access policy.
Do not assume sample stream names match your production DCR schema.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps implement Java custom log ingestion into Azure Monitor using the Azure Monitor Ingestion SDK.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It assumes you already have a Data Collection Endpoint, Data Collection Rule, workspace, and target table.

faq.question: Which authentication method is shown?
faq.answer: The examples use DefaultAzureCredential, which supports common Azure identity flows and managed identity scenarios.

faq.question: Can it support high volume uploads?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains batching, max concurrency, and asynchronous uploads, but users must test their own throughput limits.

faq.question: Does it include query guidance?
faq.answer: It only notes that azure-monitor-query can query ingested logs. Query implementation is outside this skill.

faq.question: Is this compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
